newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-INDIANS ACQUIRE SMILEY FROM REDS IN SIX-PLAYER DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-INDIANS ACQUIRE SMILEY FROM REDS IN SIX-PLAYER DEAL.

text.p: The Cleveland Indians, seeking help for an injury-riddled rotation, acquired left-handed pitcher John Smiley on Thursday in a six-player deal with the Cincinnati Reds.

The Indians sent three minor league hurlers -- right-handers Danny Graves and Scott Winchester and left-hander Jim Crowell -- to the Reds along with infielder Damian Jackson in exchange for Smiley and infielder Jeff Branson.

The 32-year-old Smiley was 9-10 with a 5.23 ERA in 20 starts for the Reds (45-60) and was on the disabled list in June with a strained left groin. Smiley, however, is 4-0 in his last five starts with a 3.18 ERA. He threw seven scoreless innings in his last start at Florida on Monday.

The Indians (54-48), who hold a three-game lead over the Milwaukee Brewers in the American League Central Division, have been forced to use 36-year-old Terry Clark and Jason Jacome as starters due to injuries to the pitching staff.
Jack McDowell, Chad Ogea and left-hander Brian Anderson are currently on Cleveland's disabled list and Albie Lopez was recently activated.
Smiley will join Charles Nagy and Orel Hershiser, who has been bothered by a strained right groin, in the starting rotation along with youngsters Bartolo Colon and Jaret Wright.
